gaps.focus: No area inventoried every on-disk writer for atomicity, crash recovery and disk-full behaviour, or checked what happens on the next launch. Go through each writer and answer: temp+rename or in place? fsync? What is left behind if the process is killed mid-write or the disk fills? Does anything on the next launch find it, report it and repair it? Writers: rps7200/library.py save() (scan.tif/raw.bin(.gz)/shading.npz/ccd_mask.bin/prescan.tif written in place, then scan.json via _write_atomic:484-491); reindex():1045-1065 (index.json via plain write_text, not atomic); rps7200/direct.py _archive_calibration ~749-803 (data.bin, then ccd_mask.bin, then shading.npz, then calibration.json, all in place; no INCOMPLETE marker and no checksum of the npz or mask); the --reference cache (direct.py:736-747); the debug spool _debug_capture:922-998 (np.save into tempfile.mkdtemp, with every exception swallowed at 997, so a partial .npy is possible on ENOSPC; is a half-written item then flushed or left?); _debug_flush:1055-1125 (rmtree with ignore_errors); rps7200/session.py write_manifest:890-922 vs the roll-folder TIFFs and prescanNN-before.tif (in place); FrameWriter._file/_unclaimed:2781-2975 (does a delivered copy that failed half-way stay under its final name, and does a retry then pick -2?); rps7200/export.py:130-190; rps7200/settings.py:88-119; rps7200/demo.py:323-325 (signature cache); tools/uniformity.py:639-647 (REJECTED and scan.json in place); tools/library.py migrate-raw:265-285. Then the launch-time sweep: does tools/gui.py or any tool detect INCOMPLETE entries, leftover `.scan.json.part`/`.part` files, orphan rps7200-debug-* spool dirs in the OS temp dir (they can be tens of GB and are never re-filed), calibration/<UTC>/ folders without calibration.json, or plain raw.bin entries left uncompacted? None of the areas checked disk-free space before a roll (no shutil.disk_usage anywhere in rps7200/ or tools/).

Write a race map across every thread and process that can touch the same files at once. Threads: the Tk UI thread, the ScanSession worker (rps7200/session.py ~1816-1976), the FrameWriter thread (~1551-1711), the debug flush (runs on the worker at close(), direct.py:1055), EdgeWatch (tools/frame_edges/watch.py:92), the demo's signing thread (demo.py ~1257) and the GUI's full-resolution/histogram/Save-all/export workers (tools/gui.py). Processes: two windows, or a window plus tools/scan_roll.py or tools/library.py on the same library/ or rolls/. For each pair, name the shared files and the lock, if any. Questions: (a) library.reindex is called from FrameWriter, from the debug flush and from the GUI's Delete-pass on the UI thread, and it writes index.json non-atomically. What does a concurrent reindex or rmtree do, especially on Windows, where it causes a sharing violation and save() then raises after the commit? (b) Is any lock taken across processes for library/, rolls/<name>/roll.json/survey.json/approved.json or gui-settings.json? RollManifest's lock is in-process only. (c) Does EdgeWatch, or the window's read_survey/read_approved, ever read a roll-folder TIFF or JSON while FrameWriter or RollManifest is rewriting it in place? The roll TIFFs are not atomic. (d) Is any numpy array that has been handed to FrameWriter or referenced by the debug spool's weakref mutated afterwards by the worker (correction, turning, mono), so that the library could receive altered 'raw' pixels? (e) Are last_pixels_raw, last_raw and last_metering read by the session after the next pass has already started?

Which is it, and would re-running the detector on the library's stored prescan give the same answer as the live run? Orientation: do the members assume an upright, unmirrored prescan, and do the window (turned/mirrored display) and scan_roll hand them the same orientation? Film types: the base colour-ratio rules (R/G 2.1-2.3, B/G ~0.53) applied to B&W/positive. Whether vote._member's abstain-on-exception hides a member that now raises on every frame. Whether the members differ from research/frame-edge beyond what the parity test (tests/test_frame_edges_parity.py, skipped in CI) would catch.

The owner's central requirement has never been checked end to end as one table. Build a matrix with one row per pass kind: window single scan, window prescan, bracket pass (tools/scan.py), roll frame, roll frame's prescan and prescan_before, metering probe rounds (auto_exposure), hold/aim verification prescans (_hold_to_approved/_aim_frame), a dry-run walk prescan, calibration, an IR pass tied and untied, a 7200 dpi stagger pass, a bottom-up pass, and a demo pass. Columns: the fields a future recomputation needs, each checked in the executable path. Those fields are the exact raw bytes; the raw_layout; MODE SELECT bytes including byte14 and filter_offsets; per-channel exposure including the IR timer; gain/offset as written and as read back; fast_ir; the scan window/frame coordinates; the SLIDE param bytes and positions of every move before the pass; the shading reference *and* a link to the calibration data.bin it was reduced from; the CCD mask; read_direction and stagger; correction state; bracket merge parameters; and the approved.json/offset decision behind the frame. Record whether the entry (scan.json/extra.commands) holds each field. Also check serialisation fidelity: library.save and calibration.json use json.dumps(default=str) (rps7200/library.py:397, direct.py:802), so np.int64/np.float32/bytes/Path values in meta become strings and lose their type. Find which meta fields actually carry such types. Then check whether reconstruct (library.py:687-774) or any test proves each row re-derivable. Existing findings cover only pieces: prescans, calibration, SLIDE bytes.

CI runs Windows, but no area checked platform-specific failure modes on the data paths. Questions: (1) Path length. Library entry ids (library.py entry_id:153-163, slug up to 40 characters plus the -N suffix), roll folder names and the delivered names from session._out_name:2908-2932 under a user's Documents/OneDrive. Can they exceed MAX_PATH 260, and what error does library.save or FrameWriter then give? (2) Case-insensitive filesystems (Windows, default macOS). A roll rename in _RollBrowser that changes only case, and two rolls whose names differ only by case, against roll_dir/new_roll_name (session.py:666, 806) and the gui-settings sheet keys by folder basename. (3) Local-time names: session.py:804 roll names and 2931-2932 output names use localtime with no zone, while library ids are UTC. What happens at a DST fold, and when rolls, entries and approved.json are joined by time? (4) The OS temp dir for the debug spool (direct.py:926). Windows Storage Sense and macOS periodic cleanup of $TMPDIR can delete a spool mid-session, and the flush then files nothing. Is this detected? (5) os.replace/rmtree on files held open by the GUI (full-resolution view, tifffile readers, np.load mmap_mode='r' at direct.py:1063) on Windows: library Delete, compact, migrate-raw. (6) packaging/60-rps7200.rules and the macOS libusb path, which no area read.

Three pieces of code were read by no area, although CLAUDE.md makes the first one mandatory before any measurement. (a) .claude/skills/measure-scan-quality/scripts/metrics.py (225 lines). Do its metrics do what the skill says: signed, channel-relative deviation rather than np.abs, dark masks, the random/fixed split from a repeat pair? Does it measure the delivered file, or does it recompute? Does it honour library.corrected's correction state, read_direction, the 7200 dpi stagger, plain raw.bin versus raw.bin.gz, and exclude demo entries? (b) tools/film_edge_study.py (424 lines). It reads scan.json with read_text() and no encoding (line 245) and writes results without an encoding (line 418), which is the only non-UTF-8-safe text IO found in the tree and fails on Windows cp1252 with non-ASCII notes. What does it select from the library, and in what orientation? (c) tools/collect_vignette_study.py (238 lines). It copies 'the five files per entry'. Does it handle entries whose raw bytes are plain raw.bin, entries still marked INCOMPLETE, the newer prescan.tif and the record's `files` checksums? Does it verify the copies against the record's sha256? And is rps7200/defects.py really dead: is it imported by any delivered path or tool?
